scope: Evidence-backed rubric-content review only; not patient advice, full clinical review, formal redteam, or task revision.

criterion.assertion: Agent recognized that LR is contraindicated or suboptimal for the DKA insulin drip (lactate metabolism concern with severe acidosis)

source_patient_record.condition: DKA, pH 7.18, glucose 486, on insulin drip
source_patient_record.fluid_need: NS 1L/hr x 2, then transition to D5-half-NS

finding: The categorical DKA/acidosis-based exclusion of lactated Ringer's is contradicted by adult consensus guidance and is not supported as a general pediatric prohibition.
confidence: High for the categorical fluid-selection premise; no case-specific treatment decision or infusion-compatibility conclusion.

primary_sources.title: Hyperglycaemic crises in adults with diabetes: a consensus report
primary_sources.publisher: Diabetologia / ADA-EASD joint consensus with JBDS, AACE and DTS endorsement
primary_sources.relevance: Permits isotonic saline or balanced crystalloids in adults without renal/cardiac compromise; names Ringer's lactate. Does not support the task's blanket acidosis-based exclusion.
primary_sources.document_kind: Endorsed expert consensus report; do not mislabel it as an ADA Standards recommendation.

primary_sources.title: 16. Diabetes Care in the Hospital: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
primary_sources.relevance: Current 2026 Standards retain saline/other crystalloid pathways adapted from the consensus; patient circumstances require individualized management.
primary_sources.access_note: Publisher search-indexed article and PDF text were accessible; direct HTML open returned an internal retrieval error.

primary_sources.title: ISPAD Clinical Practice Consensus Guidelines 2022: Diabetic ketoacidosis and hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state
primary_sources.location: Sections 6.3.2 and 6.3.3; printed page842 / PDF page8
primary_sources.relevance: Pediatric guidance specifies saline for initial resuscitation, while allowing balanced salt solutions including LR for subsequent deficit replacement. Pediatric protocols differ; this does not imply a universal LR prohibition.

primary_sources.title: Current recommendations for management of paediatric diabetic ketoacidosis
primary_sources.publisher: Canadian Paediatric Society, Acute Care Committee
primary_sources.relevance: Recognizes saline and balanced crystalloids including LR as options for pediatric DKA, with pediatric-specific monitoring and fluid protocols.

limits: The authored Bed7 record does not provide age or case-specific organ compromise; do not invent an adult/pediatric identity or a contraindication.
Saline remains an acceptable option; this finding does not assert LR is mandatory or universally superior.
Fluid resuscitation/maintenance choice is distinct from preparing insulin admixtures or establishing IV-line compatibility; those were not investigated.
This is one selected assertion, not validation of every IR-018 criterion, task fluid quantity, or protocol.
No published task, overlay, score, trajectory or historical artifact was changed.
evaluation_implication: C05 is one of ten binary criteria, uses llm_judge, and is not marked safety_critical. If faithfully enforced, disagreeing with this premise can lose one criterion and prevent all-criteria pass; no actual model grading outcome was measured in this review.
proposed_follow_up: Flag IR-018-C05 for a versioned clinical-content correction. Review linked description requiring NS and fluid_need wording together; preserve previous results and criterion denominator, and do not silently edit the published task or make new readiness claims.

preservation.provenance_note: Preserved from the earlier single-assertion review. Sources were not re-fetched during preservation. The original reviewed_at and task.git_head identify the earlier review, not a new clinical evaluation.
